item.nirncraft.dragon_claw.hint: Opens a Nordic claw door once its rings show the palm, top to bottom.
message.nirncraft.claw_door.locked: The door has a keyhole shaped like a dragon's claw: it wants the %s.
message.nirncraft.claw_door.wrong_claw: This claw doesn't fit the keyhole.
message.nirncraft.claw_door.rings: The claw won't turn. The rings must show the claw's palm, top to bottom.
message.nirncraft.puzzle.wrong: The lever won't budge, and something clicks in the walls...
book.nirncraft.dragonstone.intro: A rubbing of the Dragonstone: the burial places of the dragons, as the old priests marked them.
book.nirncraft.ustengrav_note.text:
Whoever emptied this pedestal left a scrap of parchment in its place:

"Looking for an old horn? So was I. Riverwood, the inn, the room under the roof. Come alone."
book.nirncraft.journal.barrow.0:
Day three below. The torches gutter when the wind comes up the stairs, and I swear the wind sighs a name. Brannir says the dead keep their own counsel and will not mind us borrowing a few rings.

Brannir has stopped laughing. The coffins in the long hall were shut when we passed. They are not shut now.
book.nirncraft.journal.barrow.1:
If you read this, turn back at the carved door. The pictures on the walls are not decoration: they are instructions. Bear above, then the hawk, then the snake. I had it right. I was too slow.

The ones who sleep in the walls wake when you breathe near them. Walk soft. Walk soft.
book.nirncraft.journal.barrow.2:
Note to my sister in Riverwood: the old man at the inn sold me a map of this place for six septims and told me the dragon priest had been dead four thousand years.

He was right about the dead part. He was wrong about everything that follows from it.
book.nirncraft.journal.barrow.3:
The urns are mostly ash and bone and the occasional coin. The deep hall is different. There is a wall at the end with letters cut like claw marks, and when I looked at it the letters looked back.

I have decided I do not need the gold that badly. My legs disagree; they will not carry me up the stairs.
book.nirncraft.journal.barrow.4:
Counted eleven sleepers between the antechamber and the gate. Marked each with chalk so we would know which ones had stirred.

The chalk marks are on the floor now. I did not draw them there.
book.nirncraft.journal.dwemer.0:
Field notes, third excavation. The pipes are still warm. Four thousand years with no hands to tend them and the fires burn on, which means either the Dwemer built better than we understand, or something still tends them.

The spiders have begun following me at a polite distance. I find this more alarming than if they attacked.
book.nirncraft.journal.dwemer.1:
To whoever finds my pack: the large automaton at the end of the hall does not sleep. It waits. It watched me cross the floor and did nothing, and that is how I knew it had decided I was not worth the steam.

I am going back for the strongbox anyway. A scholar must be thorough.
book.nirncraft.journal.dwemer.2: The lever by the sealed door works. I know this because I pulled it and the door opened and everything behind it woke up. Note for the next edition of my survey: do not pull the lever by the sealed door.
book.nirncraft.journal.cave.0:
Split the take three ways like we agreed, then Hrolf said three ways was too many and Ingrid agreed with him, and now it is one way, and it is me, and I have an arrow in my leg.

If you are Hrolf: the chest by the fire is empty. I moved it.
book.nirncraft.journal.cave.1:
Tracked the beast that took the Gildrin flock to this cave. Plenty of bones at the mouth, more further in, and the smell would knock a mammoth flat.

Whatever lives at the bottom is not a wolf. Wolves do not drag carts.
book.nirncraft.journal.cave.2:
Water runs somewhere below. I can hear it through the stone, and the walls glow faintly where the moss grows thick. A beautiful place to hide, if you are a thing that wants to hide.

I have been here two days. I am fairly sure I am the one hiding now.
book.nirncraft.journal.cave.3: Orders from the boss: keep the fires low, watch the tripline, and nobody goes into the back passage. Somebody went into the back passage. Now we are down to five and the boss is in a mood.
book.nirncraft.journal.mine.0:
Shift log. Vein runs east, rich as a jarl's purse. Foreman says the props will hold. Foreman also says the noises in the lower gallery are the rock settling.

Rock does not settle in a rhythm.
book.nirncraft.journal.mine.1: We dug too deep and opened a pocket of old air. The lamps burned blue for an hour. Since then the skeevers have been bolder, the carts roll on their own after dark, and Ulf will not stop humming a song none of us taught him.
book.nirncraft.journal.vampire_lair.0:
They kept us in cages by the pool and fed us well. I understood why on the second night.

If the stranger with the red eyes offers you wine, do not drink it. If you have already drunk it, find a priest of Stendarr, and run.
The master says death is a door and he merely holds the key. Today he made Sven walk again. Sven was my friend. Sven did not look at me.

I am leaving tonight. The key, it turns out, opens doors in both directions.
book.nirncraft.journal.hagraven_lair.0:
The old women of the Reach traded me a cure for my cough for a lock of hair. The cough is gone. So is my sense of taste, and I keep hearing feathers when no birds are near.

I came back to ask for my hair back. I should not have come back.
book.nirncraft.journal.fort.0:
Garrison roll, Fourth Era. Twelve men posted, nine present, two drunk, one asleep on watch. The cellar stores are short a wheel of cheese and a cask of mead, again.

The captain blames ghosts. I blame Hakon.
book.nirncraft.journal.fort.1:
They took the fort at dawn while half of us were at breakfast. I hid in the cells behind the old prisoner's bones, which is the most use those bones have been to anyone.

The new owners talk about a buyer coming from Riften. Whatever they are selling, it is locked in the deepest room.
book.nirncraft.journal.ruin.0:
The builders of this place did not think as we think. Their halls turn back on themselves, their doors open onto walls, and their dead do not lie still.

I have copied the glyphs from the tablets into this book. Match them above the door and the way opens. Get them wrong and the walls answer.
book.nirncraft.journal.ruin.1:
Three days in the dark under the old stones. Found the treasury, found the guardian, found that my sword was the wrong kind of sword.

Whoever reads this: the master of this place fears fire. Or it did. I am out of fire.
